sections.h2: Where your Chattanooga lot sits matters
sections.html:
Chattanooga is the Hamilton County seat on the Tennessee River, and its housing market is split between owners and a large renter base. Owners live in 52.4 percent of homes for 2020 to 2024, and a typical owned home is valued at $283,200. The July 1, 2025 estimate of 194,144 residents is 6.9 percent above the April 2020 base.

The city covers about 142 square miles of land, so conditions change a lot between neighborhoods. A house on a ridge, in a river-side flood area or in a historic district faces different buyer questions. Start your sale plan with where the lot sits.

Sellers who want speed usually weigh an as-is cash purchase against a conventional listing. The cash route drops repairs, showings and appraisal conditions. A listing may bring a higher price for a tidy house when the calendar allows.

Historic designation can limit what a buyer may do with a house. Ferger Place, Fort Wood and St. Elmo carry federal historic-register listings, and the city also has local historic districts including Battery Place, Glenwood, Missionary Ridge, M.L. King and Stringer's Ridge. Ask the Land Development Office whether a local district covers your address before you promise a buyer any exterior renovation.

  • Downtown and the North Shore sit near the Tennessee Aquarium, the Walnut Street Bridge and Coolidge Park.
  • The M.L. King district runs beside the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga campus.
  • Hixson, Highland Park and Lookout Valley, also called Tiftonia, are separate communities within the city limits.
  • East of Missionary Ridge, Brainerd Road and East Brainerd Road carry traffic toward Hamilton Place.

Public schools fall under Hamilton County Schools. Check which zone an address falls in before quoting school information to a buyer.

Buyers' inspectors check roof condition, tree cover and drainage, and a seller who fixed those items in advance gets a cleaner negotiation. Hilly lots bring their own checks, and you can prepare a short file for them:

  • Retaining wall and drainage work, with contractor invoices.
  • Engineer letters on foundations built on sloped ground.
  • Driveway grade and access details for steep lots.

Keep that file ready so it can go out with the first offer.

sections.h2: Chattanooga property tax and due dates
sections.html:
The City Council sets the city rate, which is $1.93 per hundred dollars of assessed value. Homes are assessed at 25 percent and commercial parcels at 40 percent. Hamilton County taxes come on top.

Notices go out in September, taxes are due October 1, and payment stays penalty-free until the last day of February. From March 1, interest and penalty total 1.5 percent a month. Delinquent prior-year taxes are filed in Hamilton County Chancery Court each March, and a property can be sold after three years of delinquency.

The City Treasurer is at Room 100, 101 E. 11th Street, 423-643-7262. Do not count on a mailed notice reaching you, because a lost bill does not excuse a late payment. Pull a copy from the city's property tax search before closing.

sections.h2: Tax freeze for homeowners 65 and older
sections.html:
Homeowners 65 or older can apply for the city's Tax Freeze, which holds the city portion of the bill steady for one year. The combined 2025 income limit is $63,470, and the home must be the primary residence. The 2026 application deadline is April 5, 2027.

The freeze covers city taxes only. County taxes and fees such as stormwater are not frozen, and the owner has to reapply every year or the taxes revert to the current rate and value. Applicants submit proof of ownership, residency, age and income. The Senior Programs line is 423-643-7274.

Until closing day, keep the application current, since a lapse returns your city bill to the current rate and value.

sections.h2: How do I dispute a Hamilton County value?
sections.html:
Request an informal review from the Hamilton County Assessor of Property first. Useful proof includes sales prices of similar properties in the immediate area within the last three years, a recent private appraisal and photos. Results are mailed.

Phone the Assessor at 423-209-7300, weekdays between 8 and 4:30, to ask when the next review window opens. Properties are reappraised every four years. When the informal review fails, the county equalization board takes appeals, reached at the same number.

After a denial at the county level, you can file with the state until August 1 of the tax year or within 45 days of the local notice, whichever is later.

You can host short-term guests only with a city certificate, and the zoning rules are tight. A homestay is owner-occupied for at least 183 days a year and costs $250 to apply or renew. An absentee rental costs $500 and is allowed only in commercial zones C-C, C-R, C-MU1 and C-MU2 and form-based zones CC, CX, IX, RF, RV and SH.

Certificates last one year, and the Board of Zoning Appeals cannot exceed the 25 percent density cap. Applications have a 60-day life from submission, and a rezoned property cannot get an absentee certificate for 18 months. For a seller, the useful rule is that a valid certificate can be transferred to a new owner of the same address, though the occupancy type cannot change. Call the Land Development Office at 423-643-5891 with questions.

sections.h2: Filing the deed and state charges
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds office, in the courthouse at 625 Georgia Avenue (Room 400), takes Chattanooga deeds at 423-209-6560 on weekdays from 8 until 4. It records deeds and similar instruments and collects the fees and taxes attached to them.

The state's realty transfer tax is 37 cents per $100 of price. A separate mortgage tax of 11.5 cents per $100 applies to borrowed amounts above the first $2,000. Request the full cost list from the title company before the closing date.

Gather your payoff letters, your latest tax notice and the names of every owner on the deed before you set a date. Co-owner signatures and lien payoffs cause most delays, and a cash buyer with a clean title can close much faster than a listing that depends on a lender.

faqs.q: How soon can a Chattanooga cash sale close?
faqs.a: Closing is possible within about two weeks when title is clear and any estate or lien paperwork is ready. The Hamilton County Register of Deeds files the deed after signing. Delays usually come from payoff letters and co-owner signatures.

faqs.q: What is the Chattanooga city property tax rate?
faqs.a: The city rate is $1.93 per hundred dollars of assessed value, with homes assessed at 25 percent of appraisal. Hamilton County tax is separate, so ask the Trustee at 423-209-7270 for the county rate.

faqs.q: Who covers the state transfer tax on a Chattanooga sale?
faqs.a: The rate is 37 cents per $100 of price, collected at recording. Your purchase contract says who is responsible, and the title company shows the amount on the closing statement.

faqs.q: Does a vacation rental certificate pass to a buyer?
faqs.a: Yes. It can move to the new owner of the same property when the buyer files the transfer application. It cannot follow the operator to a different address, and the occupancy type stays the same.

faqs.q: When does Hamilton County reappraise next?
faqs.a: Properties are reappraised every four years. Call the Hamilton County Assessor at 423-209-7300 for the next effective date.
